scope: Proposition 5.4 (The period coordinate) of the manuscript “Exact Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer Formula from Low Selmer Corank” (preprints/Exact-Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer-Formula-from-Low-Selmer-Corank-October-7-2026/exact-bsd-low-selmer-corank.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 002 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 64b46603e174462e), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 31. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: In square or unfilled rectangular order, for every finite even character ν of conductor dividing M, the coordinate of exp∗(zν) in ω, in compatible field realizations, is ±∆ν L(M)(f, ν, 1) Ω0 δξ(a), ∆ν = (c2 − cν(c)−1 )(d2 − dν(d)−1 ). (2) The superscript omits all primes dividing M, and the sign is common across symbols. In square order with A = 1, an integral combination has δ(a) = 1. In rectangular order, some choice of A = pk and ξ with lower row (Ns, 1) has δξ(a) ̸= 0.
